data.name: SqlRejectForUpdate
data.value: SELECT … FOR UPDATE locks rows – FerretSharp only sets locks when editing.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectEmpty
data.value: No statement at the cursor.

data.name: SqlRejectDataLoss
data.value: The SQL editor does not run statements that delete rows or dropped objects without a way back: TRUNCATE or DROP of partitions, FLASHBACK TABLE to an earlier point (TO BEFORE DROP is fine), PURGE, DROP TABLE … PURGE (past the recycle bin), DROP USER … CASCADE. Use DELETE instead – it stays in the transaction.

data.name: SqlRejectTruncate
data.value: The SQL editor does not run TRUNCATE: it deletes every row and cannot be undone. Use DELETE instead – it stays in the transaction.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectPlSqlObject
data.value: The SQL editor does not create PL/SQL objects (procedures, functions, packages, types) yet – only triggers.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement: CREATE [OR REPLACE] PROCEDURE …

data.name: SqlRejectSystemTrigger
data.value: The SQL editor does not create triggers on the database or a schema (ON DATABASE, ON SCHEMA) – they fire on every logon or every DDL. Only triggers on a table or view.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement: CREATE TRIGGER … AFTER LOGON ON DATABASE

data.name: SqlRejectDdlBinds
data.value: DDL takes no bind variables (:{0}) – write the value into the statement.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement. {0} = name of the first bind variable, without the colon

data.name: SqlRejectPlSql
data.value: The SQL editor does not run PL/SQL blocks or procedure calls – they can commit on their own.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectTransactionControl
data.value: Use the status bar for {0} (Commit, Rollback).
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement. {0} = first word of the statement, e.g. COMMIT

data.name: SqlRejectSessionControl
data.value: ALTER SESSION/SYSTEM changes the workspace’s session and is not run.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectLock
data.value: LOCK TABLE is not run – FerretSharp only sets locks when editing.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectExplain
data.value: Use the “Plan” button for execution plans.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run EXPLAIN PLAN. “Plan” is the label of the button in the SQL editor's toolbar.

data.name: SqlRejectOther
data.value: The SQL editor does not run “{0}” – only SELECT, WITH, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement. {0} = first word of the statement

data.name: SqlPlanReadOnly

data.name: SqlPlanReadOnlyDdl

data.name: SqlPlanDmlBeforeDdl
data.value: {0} (DDL) would commit the changes of statement {1} implicitly. Put the DDL before the DML or run them separately.
data.comment: A script has DML before DDL. {0} = first word of the DDL statement, e.g. CREATE; {1} = number of the DML statement in the script

data.name: SqlPlanStatementProblem
